operationalization: Compile observations of defensive inking after standardized threats across octopuses, squids and cuttlefish, and compare discharge volume relative to body mass. Any non-inking species refutes the universal claim; consistently greatest relative volume in cuttlefish supports the comparison.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: species identities, ecology and life-history records for cephalopods

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: species-level behavioral accounts and source links

obstacles: Ink volume and eliciting threat are not standardized in broad databases.
The universal quantifier requires unusually complete taxonomic coverage.
rationale: Defensive inking and discharge amount are measurable, but observations are dispersed through species accounts and experiments. Existing evidence can test major clades and the cuttlefish comparison, not confidently every cephalopod.

operationalization: Count thoracic appendages, treating chelipeds as the first walking-leg pair, in identified spiny lobsters and true crabs. Ten appendages supports the claim, while a consistent different count refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: open specimen imagery and 3D media for appendage counts

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: modern taxonomy for spiny lobsters and brachyuran crabs

obstacles: Damaged museum specimens can be missing legs.
rationale: The characters are standard decapod anatomy and can be scored directly from abundant public specimen media and taxonomic descriptions. The result cleanly distinguishes ten limbs from alternative counts.

operationalization: Measure left and right chela dimensions in sexed Homarus specimens, define a preregistered equality tolerance, and estimate the frequency of symmetric animals by sex. Any verified equal-clawed individual refutes the absolute statement.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media usable for bilateral claw measurements

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: occurrence and taxonomic context for Homarus sampling

obstacles: Public images often omit sex and measurement scale.
Regenerated claws can confound innate asymmetry.
rationale: The prediction is precise and falsifiable, but no broad open table appears to pair sex with bilateral claw measurements. Public specimens and literature permit a substantial sample, though not a decisive census of both species and sexes.

operationalization: For a taxonomically broad sample of brachyuran specimens, score which chela is larger and test whether right-handed individuals exceed 50%. A majority on the right supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public crab specimen media for chela laterality

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: accepted brachyuran taxonomy

obstacles: Laterality varies strongly among crab families.
Images and specimens are not sampled randomly for handedness.
rationale: Laterality is straightforward to score, and a majority criterion is discriminating. Existing open media are biased and do not provide representative coverage of brachyurans, so only restricted taxonomic tests are currently feasible.

operationalization: Map 'stromboid testaceans' to gastropod taxa, score shell coiling as dextral or sinistral from specimens, and separately code locomotor direction relative to the spire. A sinistral member refutes the universal coiling statement.

candidate_datasets.name: MolluscaBase
candidate_datasets.role: accepted gastropod names and taxonomic scope

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: shell media for coiling direction

obstacles: The ancient category 'stromboid' has several modern interpretations.
Locomotor direction is rarely encoded in specimen datasets.
rationale: Shell handedness is easily resolved with public collections, including known exceptions to universal dextrality. The locomotion clause and ancient taxonomic boundary are much less directly represented, making the combined claim only partial.

operationalization: Identify the named predatory gastropods and compile observations or shell traces showing proboscis-associated drilling through prey shells. Repeated direct observations and diagnostic boreholes support the claim; absence of drilling with a different feeding mechanism refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: diet and feeding ecology records for marine gastropods

candidate_datasets.name: MolluscaBase
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic mapping of murex and trumpet-shell names

obstacles: Predatory drilling may involve the radula and accessory boring organ rather than the proboscis alone.
Behavioral evidence is spread across papers.
rationale: Drilled prey shells and feeding behavior are observable and strongly discriminating. Public databases establish taxa and ecology, while mechanism-specific data require literature compilation and may reveal that the stated anatomy is oversimplified.

operationalization: The anatomical resemblance and shell-occupying habit can be measured, but no observation uniquely decides whether those traits make the hermit crab 'intermediate' between Aristotle's kinds.
obstacles: 'Intermediate' is a classificatory judgment without a quantitative decision rule.
The compared ancient categories do not correspond to sister modern taxa.
rationale: The component facts are empirically documentable, but the central conclusion depends on Aristotle's classification. Different weighting of morphology and habit can yield either classification without any new observation deciding between them.

operationalization: Mouth position, anus position and benthic feeding can be recorded, but those observations do not distinguish adaptive final placement from a non-teleological developmental explanation.
obstacles: The phrase 'because it is best suited' supplies no rival-sensitive prediction.
The anatomical fact used as evidence is also what the explanation seeks to explain.
rationale: Existing data readily confirm the orientation and feeding substrate, but mere fit does not test the final-cause explanation. No stated measurable consequence separates that explanation from developmental or phylogenetic alternatives.

operationalization: Count gonads in dissected or imaged sea-urchin specimens across representative taxa and developmental anomalies. Five in every normal specimen supports the statement; any authenticated normal specimen with another count refutes 'always'.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D and specimen media showing echinoid internal anatomy

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic coverage of Echinoidea

obstacles: Abnormal individuals require a prespecified inclusion rule.
rationale: Gonad number is a standard and conspicuous echinoid character. Public anatomical resources plus taxonomic descriptions provide broad coverage, and a non-five count gives a direct falsification.

operationalization: Measure solid and dissolved waste release from identified sea anemones while feeding, and compare presence of egestion or nitrogenous excretion with plants under a stated definition. Detecting waste products refutes the no-excretion clause.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: species ecology and feeding records for sea anemones

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: modern taxonomic mapping of Actiniaria

obstacles: 'Excretion' could mean feces, metabolic excretion, or a dedicated outlet.
Physiological flux data are scattered across experiments.
rationale: Waste release is measurable, but the ancient term is ambiguous and the plant resemblance is qualitative. Existing physiological literature can resolve particular species and definitions, not the full category as phrased.

operationalization: Define a standardized bisection plane and survival interval, then compare post-bisection survival across insect orders, body sizes and temperatures. Failure to survive in warm, sufficiently large insects would refute the qualified universal.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic sampling frame for insect diversity

obstacles: No broad public dataset records survival after experimental bisection.
The exceptions 'cold by nature' and 'chill quickly' are not operationally specified.
A representative test would require new experiments.
rationale: The survival outcome is testable after substantial clarification, but occurrence and trait databases do not contain the required intervention. Isolated reports cannot adequately cover the stated scope of all insects.

operationalization: Map two-winged insects to Diptera and inspect adult posterior abdominal anatomy across families for a true sting. One dipteran with a homologous posterior sting refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public insect specimen imagery and scans

candidate_datasets.name: Catalogue of Life
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic sampling frame for Diptera

obstacles: Piercing ovipositors and biting mouthparts must be distinguished from stings.
Public anatomy media are uneven across dipteran families.
rationale: The statement has a clear anatomical interpretation and a decisive counterexample criterion. Existing collections can cover many families, but proving absence across the enormous order remains limited by uneven anatomical annotation.

operationalization: Code cicada mouthparts, food sources from feeding observations or plant-DNA/chemical evidence, and gut or waste contents. Functional mouthparts, feeding on xylem rather than dew, or excretion refutes the corresponding clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts and referenced feeding traits for cicadas

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media for cicada mouthpart anatomy

obstacles: No single open dataset joins mouthpart, diet and excretion observations.

operationalization: A test would require a non-circular criterion for individuating senses; without one, detecting magnetoreception, electroreception or proprioception can be redescribed as touch or as a new sense.
obstacles: The number depends on how sensory modalities are defined and grouped.
The phrase 'special sense' lacks an empirical identity criterion.
rationale: Animals have measurable sensory channels beyond the traditional five, but whether each counts as a separate sense is conceptual. Data alone cannot settle the asserted total without first choosing a taxonomy of senses.

operationalization: Use histology and 3D anatomical images of Talpa eyes to score external visibility, size and presence of canonical ocular structures. Missing canonical parts or exposed normal-sized eyes refute the stated anatomy.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public 3D and specimen media for mammalian cranial anatomy

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts and referenced anatomical descriptions

obstacles: 'All parts' needs a defined list of ocular structures.
rationale: Mole eye reduction is standard comparative anatomy with abundant archived specimens and published histology. The core claims of hidden position, reduction and structural completeness can be directly checked with existing material.

operationalization: Compile auditory and olfactory organs and behavioral or electrophysiological responses to controlled sound and odor stimuli across fishes. Responses above controls support hearing and smell; anatomical evidence tests the 'no visible organs' qualifier.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: species biology and sensory ecology references for fishes

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: fish anatomical scans showing internal sensory structures

obstacles: Startle to galley noise alone may also involve vibration or lateral-line detection.

operationalization: Modern invertebrate diversity can be assigned to Aristotle's four bins only after choosing definitions; no observation determines that these rather than another set are the correct genera.
obstacles: The four kinds are an ancient classificatory scheme, not an exhaustive measurable hypothesis.
Modern taxa such as flatworms and cnidarians do not map uniquely to the bins.
rationale: Species traits and phylogeny could expose omissions, but 'with very few exceptions' has no threshold and the categories are stipulated. The core claim concerns classification and cannot be resolved independently of a chosen scheme.

operationalization: Define voice as actively generated communication sound, then code lung presence, sound-production anatomy and recordings across animals. A lungless animal producing such sound without a pharynx refutes the universal mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public animal sound recordings

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: biology of sound-producing marine animals

obstacles: 'Voice' can be restricted by definition to pulmonary phonation.
Sound archives do not systematically encode production mechanisms.
rationale: The claim becomes testable under a behaviorally neutral definition of voice, and public recordings include many lungless sound producers. Mechanism and anatomy must be compiled separately, so broad resolution is possible but not turnkey.

operationalization: Measure gas exchange and ventilatory airflow through insect spiracles and tracheae, and identify sound-production mechanisms. Demonstrated active respiratory ventilation refutes 'no insect breathes,' while mechanism data test whether sound depends on expelled air.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts and references on insect respiration and sound production

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: insect anatomical media for tracheal and sound-producing structures

obstacles: 'Breathes' may mean lung breathing rather than any respiration.

rationale: Gas exchange and ventilation are directly measurable and extensively studied, but ancient terminology creates an interpretation choice. Existing data resolve representative mechanisms well, with incomplete order-wide coverage.

operationalization: Predefine language by measurable features such as compositional syntax, displaced reference and open-ended productivity, then code controlled communication studies in humans and other mammals. A nonhuman system meeting all criteria refutes uniqueness under that definition.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public comparative animal vocal recordings

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: large public collection of animal vocalizations

Recordings alone rarely establish semantics or syntax.
Controlled cognition data are sparse and heterogeneous.
rationale: Some consequences of the uniqueness claim can be tested, but the verdict depends heavily on a prior definition of language. Existing recordings and experiments test restricted features rather than the full philosophical contrast.

operationalization: Compare songs of cross-fostered or acoustically isolated juveniles with tutors and genetic parents, and quantify geographic song variation. Tutor matching and locality effects beyond genetic structure support learned modification.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: georeferenced bird recordings for dialect analysis

candidate_datasets.name: Xeno-canto
candidate_datasets.role: public georeferenced bird-song recordings

candidate_datasets.name: OpenNeuro
candidate_datasets.role: public neurophysiology datasets, including sleep studies where available

Physiological proxies do not uniquely imply dream experience.
Open comparative coverage is poor outside laboratory species.
rationale: Existing sleep physiology can test dream-like neural states in several mammals, but the universal claim and subjective interpretation remain underdetermined. Behavioral barking is suggestive rather than decisive.

operationalization: Define sleep by reversible quiescence, elevated arousal threshold and homeostatic rebound, then compile duration measurements for fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans. Sleep in each clade supports the first clause; durations comparable to or longer than other animals refute 'very short'.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: species-level ecology and behavior for marine animals

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish behavior and ecology records

Duration data are concentrated in a few model species.

operationalization: Analyze tagged or video-recorded cetacean sleep bouts for blowhole position relative to the surface, breathing and fin movement. Submerged sleep or immobile sleep in a blowhole-bearing species refutes the corresponding universal clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic and occurrence context for cetacean coverage

operationalization: Map sessile animals and testaceans to modern taxa and code gonochorism, hermaphroditism and asexual reproduction from reproductive records. Any sessile or shelled taxon with separate males and females refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic mapping of marine sessile and shelled animals

operationalization: Inspect sexed Anguilla specimens and reproductive datasets for ovaries, testes, gametes, spawning and offspring. Any verified male, female, egg or successful reproduction refutes the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility

operationalization: Join adult body mass, sex and longevity across mammals and compare sex ratios of those traits with analogous size data for fishes, insects, reptiles, spiders and frogs using phylogenetic models. Directional majorities support each 'general rule'.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: sex-specific and species-level longevity records

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open animal trait records including body size and life history

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase

candidate_datasets.name: Shark-References

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public specimen images and scans of chondrichthyans

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public vertebrate anatomy images and 3D scans

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: referenced reproductive anatomy accounts

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web

obstacles: No known public dataset records controlled non-contact impregnation treatments.

obstacles: The common pigeon may include domestic forms with large size variation.
rationale: Body size is directly measured and comprehensive open bird trait data include the likely species. Alternative mappings can be sensitivity-tested with the same straightforward rank comparison.

operationalization: Within individuals, compare fertilization success and offspring or egg size from the first mature ejaculate or clutch with later ones, stratified by taxon. Equal or better first reproductive output refutes the asserted universal deterioration.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public research datasets that may contain clutch order and reproductive outcomes

obstacles: 'Earliest semen' is ambiguous between puberty, season and mating sequence.
Longitudinal first-reproduction data are sparse and dispersed.
The claim spans very different reproductive systems.
rationale: A within-individual design is possible, but substantial interpretation is required and no cross-animal dataset contains the variables directly. Existing studies can resolve selected humans, domestic mammals or birds only.

operationalization: Estimate age distributions for spermarche, viable sperm production and achieved paternity in male humans. Medians or stated percentiles near fourteen and twenty-one support the two age claims; materially different distributions refute them.

candidate_datasets.name: Demographic and Health Surveys
candidate_datasets.role: public survey microdata on male fertility and age at first fatherhood where available

candidate_datasets.name: UK Data Service
candidate_datasets.role: public and safeguarded longitudinal human puberty and fertility datasets

obstacles: Age at first fatherhood is affected by social behavior and is not biological capability.
Spermarche and sperm viability are not in the same datasets.
rationale: The ages and outcomes can be defined quantitatively, and existing public health and longitudinal records cover puberty and realized fertility. Separate physiological and demographic datasets are needed, but standard analyses can resolve the approximate statements.

operationalization: Extract fundamental frequency from sexed, age-labeled recordings within species and fit phylogenetically structured sex and age effects. Predominantly higher female and juvenile pitch supports the general rule.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: large public collection of animal vocal recordings

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public identified animal sounds

obstacles: Sex and age metadata are missing for many recordings.
Fundamental frequency depends on call type and behavioral context.
Archive sampling is not representative of all vocal animals.
rationale: Pitch has a standard acoustic measure and public recordings permit many within-species comparisons. Metadata and sampling limitations prevent a clean test of the unrestricted cross-animal majority.

operationalization: Measure fundamental frequency from comparable calls of adult cows, bulls and calves, controlling breed and context. Lower female than male and lower calf than adult frequencies support the two reversals.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public cattle vocal recordings

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: additional public mammal recordings

obstacles: Public recordings may lack breed, sex, age or call-context metadata.
Call types differ between calves and adults.
rationale: The acoustic comparison is direct and discriminating, but currently available archives are not designed as balanced cattle experiments. Existing recordings can test subsets, while a definitive matched analysis may require curated data.

operationalization: Compare acoustic pitch and prespecified secondary sexual traits in intact males, castrated males and females, controlling age and species. Movement of castrated males toward female trait values supports the specific measurable consequences.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public mammal vocal recordings where sex and condition are documented

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public experimental and veterinary datasets on castration effects

obstacles: 'Characters of the female' is too broad without a fixed trait list.
Age at castration and hormone treatment are major confounders.
Open matched datasets are uncommon.
rationale: Voice change and selected morphology are measurable, but the general feminization mechanism is vague. Existing veterinary and acoustic data can test particular species and traits rather than all male characters.

operationalization: Analyze mating- or ovulation-dated canine pregnancies for birth timing and neonatal survival. The gestation distribution tests 60–63 days, and surviving litters born before 60 days refute the survival exception.

candidate_datasets.name: VetCompass
candidate_datasets.role: large veterinary clinical data resource for dogs

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public veterinary research datasets with canine reproduction records

obstacles: Gestation length differs depending on whether mating, ovulation or hormone surge starts the clock.
rationale: Gestation and survival are standard clinical variables with extensive existing canine records. Explicitly defining the start event permits a direct distributional test with adequate sample size.

operationalization: Estimate sex-specific horse lifespan and age-specific reproductive success from pedigree and longevity records. Means or survival quantiles near 35 and over 40, with reproduction near the lifespan limit, support the statement.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: horse longevity records and references

candidate_datasets.name: Domestic Animal Diversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: public breed and domestic-animal information

obstacles: Ancient husbandry conditions differ greatly from modern managed horses.
Maximum, mean and typical lifespan must be distinguished.
rationale: Sex, lifespan and reproductive age are directly measurable, and existing equine demographic records are substantial. Historical-population transportability is limited, but the biological claim about domestic horses can be analyzed now.

operationalization: Use age-specific births by maternal and paternal age to estimate typical and upper reproductive limits, distinguishing biological capability from observed reproduction. Frequent births beyond the proposed limits refute them; rare tails test the stated maxima.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Fertility Database
candidate_datasets.role: public age-specific fertility rates across populations

candidate_datasets.name: Demographic and Health Surveys
candidate_datasets.role: public survey microdata on births and parental ages

obstacles: Observed paternity at old ages is shaped by partnership and contraception.
Modern assisted reproduction can alter upper limits.
rationale: Large public demographic datasets directly contain maternal age and often paternal age at birth. Standard survival or rate analyses can resolve typical ages and quantify rare exceptions, with social confounding noted.

operationalization: Compile breeding records for dromedaries with conception and birth dates and litter size. A gestation distribution centered near twelve months and singleton births support the claim; verified twins refute 'never'.

candidate_datasets.name: Domestic Animal Diversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: public information on domestic camel breeds

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: camel reproductive life-history records and references

obstacles: Breed and husbandry affect gestation estimates.
Rare twinning requires a large sample to assess an absolute claim.
rationale: Gestation duration and litter size are routine husbandry variables with extensive existing records. Even rare counterexamples can decisively test the absolute singleton clause.

operationalization: Analyze conception- and birth-dated elephant records for gestation length and litter size across elephant species. The distribution tests the two-year approximation, while any twin birth refutes strict uniparity.

candidate_datasets.name: Species360
candidate_datasets.role: zoo demographic and reproductive records, with public summary resources

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: elephant gestation and life-history records

obstacles: Individual-level Species360 access may be restricted.
Rare twins require large historical samples.
rationale: Elephant gestation and litter size are exceptionally well documented in existing zoo and field records. Public summaries and life-history databases suffice to evaluate both approximate duration and the claimed singleton pattern.

operationalization: For Bolinus brandaris and Hexaplex trunculus, compare known-age or mark-recaptured lifespan with counts of shell growth intervals validated against annual chronology. Agreement at one interval per year and survival near six years supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MolluscaBase
candidate_datasets.role: accepted taxonomy for candidate purple murex species

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: murex longevity and growth references

obstacles: Shell increments may record spawning or environmental events rather than years.
Validated known-age series are sparse.
Two candidate species may differ.
rationale: Both lifespan and increment periodicity are measurable, but open known-age validation data are limited. Existing growth studies can test particular populations without fully resolving the two-species historical identification.

operationalization: Compare survival of Pinna nobilis naturally or experimentally with and without Pontonia shrimp or pea crabs, controlling disease and habitat. Similar survival without commensals refutes dependence; elevated rapid mortality supports it.

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: co-occurrence and distribution records for Pinna and commensals

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: accepted identities of host and commensal species

obstacles: Co-occurrence does not identify causal dependence.
Pinna nobilis is critically endangered and affected by mass mortality disease.
Public survival data with commensal status are scarce.
rationale: The mortality consequence is clear, but current occurrence records only establish association. Existing scattered observations may test some naturally unoccupied hosts; a clean causal estimate would likely require data not presently assembled.

operationalization: For oysters, cockles, mussels, scallops, limpets, ascidians and barnacles, compile gametes, larvae, parentage and settlement records. Evidence that settlers arise from sexual or asexual propagules rather than mud refutes spontaneous generation, while substrate data separately test habitat associations.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproduction, larval development and habitat records

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: DNA barcodes linking larval and adult life stages

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic mapping of the disparate testacean groups

obstacles: The ancient category combines several unrelated phyla.
rationale: The proposed origin mechanism has clear ancestry predictions and is contradicted or supported by abundant existing life-cycle data. Substrate preferences can also be analyzed independently without new collection.

operationalization: Define egg growth as increasing external volume or dry biomass after oviposition, then compare serial measurements through development in crustaceans, cephalopods and oviparous fishes. No increase or shrinkage in included taxa refutes universality.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: marine egg and reproductive development records

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish egg size and reproductive records

obstacles: Apparent volume increase can be water uptake rather than biological growth.
Serial egg measurements are not standardized across taxa.
The translation's 'molluscs' primarily means cephalopods.
rationale: A measurable size criterion is possible but may not preserve Aristotle's meaning of growth. Existing embryology data cover many species, though not a representative sample of all three broad groups.

operationalization: Compile validated lifespan distributions for squid, cuttlefish and octopus species and estimate the fraction surviving beyond one year. A substantial frequency of multi-year species refutes the broad 'few exceptions' statement.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: cephalopod longevity and life-history records

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: validated longevity records for animal species

obstacles: Age estimation methods differ among cephalopod groups.
Deep-sea and large species are underrepresented.
'Few exceptions' requires a threshold.
rationale: Lifespan is a standard trait with many existing estimates, and the one-year boundary is explicit. Coverage biases and the unspecified exception rate limit resolution of the whole class-level statement.

operationalization: Use lineage tracing and developmental imaging to test whether adult tissues differentiate from cells distributed through the larva or from a localized subset, and separately code egg versus larval development across insects. Localized imaginal-disc origins would refute a literal whole-grub claim.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public developmental microscopy datasets

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public developmental expression and cell-lineage datasets

obstacles: 'The whole grub becomes the animal' can mean organismal continuity rather than contribution of every tissue.
Molecular datasets are concentrated in model insects.
rationale: Modern developmental imaging can test tissue contribution in detail for model insects. The all-insects preface and ambiguity between organismal and cellular continuity prevent complete resolution as stated.

operationalization: Compile life cycles of human tapeworms, roundworms and pinworms, identifying whether eggs produced by intestinal adults develop into conspecific descendants. Viable conspecific offspring refute the no-propagation claim.

candidate_datasets.name: CDC DPDx
candidate_datasets.role: public parasite life-cycle and diagnostic data

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: sequence records linking parasite life stages and species

obstacles: Some parasites require an intermediate host, which can obscure direct succession in the intestine.
rationale: Parasite reproduction and eggs are directly observable, and authoritative public life-cycle resources cover all three named forms. The result decisively distinguishes reproduction from spontaneous origin.

operationalization: Measure ingestion and fecal output during larval and pupal stages of butterflies, bees and wasps. Feeding or defecation by a normal pupa refutes the pupal clause; larval feeding and excretion support the contrast.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: insect life-history accounts and references

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public developmental imaging datasets for insects

obstacles: Meconium released at adult emergence must be distinguished from pupal defecation.
rationale: Stage-specific feeding and excretion are elementary observable traits of holometabolous development. Existing life-history and developmental data provide broad coverage and a clear decision rule.

operationalization: Interpret generation as initiation of development, then compare parentage and developmental rates under temperature and airflow manipulations. Genetic parental origin refutes heat or wind as a primary generative source, while temperature effects test a weaker developmental role.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: genetic records supporting parentage and life-stage continuity

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public insect thermal-development datasets

obstacles: 'Due primarily' conflates causal origin with environmental acceleration.
Wind could mean dispersal rather than biological generation.
Thermal data are taxonomically uneven.
rationale: The spontaneous-origin reading is strongly testable with existing life-cycle evidence, while a weaker claim about environmental control is also measurable. Ambiguous causal wording prevents a single decisive operationalization.

operationalization: Survey operating copper-smelting furnaces in Cyprus for the described winged organism, document temperature exposure and survival away from heat, and identify specimens genetically. Absence after adequate sampling or inability to survive furnace temperatures would refute the report.
obstacles: The organism is unnamed and cannot be linked confidently to a modern taxon.
No known public dataset samples fauna inside Cypriot smelting fires.
Historical smelting conditions may no longer exist.
rationale: The described observations are measurable in principle, but there is no adequate existing dataset and the target cannot be reliably identified. A meaningful test requires new field sampling or historical specimens.

operationalization: For candidate spider wasps and mud daubers, code prey capture, whether spiders are dead or paralyzed, nest material, egg placement and offspring emergence. Observations matching all stages support the sequence; living paralyzed prey or eggs rather than grubs at provisioning refute details.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: species behavior accounts and references for Pompilidae and mud daubers

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
candidate_datasets.role: occurrence and taxonomic records for candidate wasps

obstacles: Aristotle's 'ichneumon' may cover multiple wasp lineages.
Behavioral sequences are mostly in dispersed natural-history observations.
rationale: The nesting sequence has clear observable stages and extensive existing natural-history evidence. Taxon ambiguity and lack of a unified behavioral dataset limit comprehensive assessment.

operationalization: Trace isotopically or chemically the inputs to wax and honey and observe bee collection and processing of nectar. Honey derived from floral nectar transformed by bees refutes atmospheric-dew origin; wax-gland secretion tests the flower-to-wax mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public honey-bee gland and metabolic expression datasets

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: honey-bee feeding and wax-production accounts with sources

obstacles: Existing evidence is distributed across chemical, behavioral and physiological studies.
rationale: The alternative material sources make distinct chemical and behavioral predictions. Extensive existing data on nectar processing and wax glands can resolve both clauses using standard analyses.

operationalization: Analyze survival distributions separately for worker, drone, queen and colony identities. Typical lifespan near six years and a seven-year maximum supports the claim under the relevant interpretation; longer survival refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: BEEHAVE
candidate_datasets.role: open honey-bee colony model and empirical parameter resources

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: honey-bee caste and colony longevity accounts

obstacles: 'The bee' may mean an individual queen, worker, or the colony.
Longevity differs by caste by orders of magnitude.
Open longitudinal colony survival records are heterogeneous.
rationale: Lifespan is measurable and existing data cover bees and colonies, but the subject is critically ambiguous. Each interpretation can be tested, yet they produce very different verdicts on the numerical statement.

operationalization: Compile continuous brood observations for scorpions and spiders, scoring maternal survival and whether offspring directly attack and kill her. Surviving mothers or death from unrelated causes refute the generalized behavior.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: species natural-history accounts and source references

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic sampling frame for scorpions and spiders

obstacles: Matriphagy occurs in some spiders but not broadly.
Behavioral observations are sparse and publication-biased.
The land-scorpion identity is broad.
rationale: Maternal killing is directly observable, and existing species accounts can reveal both occurrences and counterexamples. Open systematic brood-level data are too limited for the full groups.

operationalization: For Mediterranean grasshopper species, use dated oviposition and adult survival records to test whether laying peaks at summer's end and whether both sexes die shortly afterward. Persistent adults or other laying seasons refute the generalization.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
candidate_datasets.role: dated grasshopper occurrences and life-stage annotations where available

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: grasshopper life-cycle accounts and references

obstacles: Most occurrence records lack oviposition or reproductive status.
Grasshopper phenology varies among species and climates.
Death after laying requires individual follow-up.
rationale: Season and survival are measurable, and existing phenology records test common regional species. The causal sequence and broad taxonomic claim are not adequately represented in public structured data.

operationalization: Link sexed cicada specimens to sound production and tymbal anatomy across the large and small candidate species. Female calling or male silence as a sex-wide anatomical pattern would refute the stated dimorphism.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public cicada sound recordings

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: identified insect sound recordings

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media for sound-producing anatomy

obstacles: Recording metadata do not always identify the emitting individual's sex.
rationale: Calling and tymbal anatomy are conspicuous, sex-linked traits with extensive recordings and specimens. Existing data permit a direct test across plausible species mappings.

operationalization: Identify whether the 'nits' of lice, fleas and bedbugs are eggs and follow them through hatching and reproduction. Development into conspecific offspring directly refutes the statement that they generate nothing.

candidate_datasets.name: CDC DPDx
candidate_datasets.role: public ectoparasite identification and life-cycle information

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: DNA barcode records for ectoparasite life stages

obstacles: The word 'nit' is normally restricted to louse eggs and may be applied loosely here.
rationale: Egg identity, hatching and life-cycle continuity are elementary observations with extensive existing public documentation. Testing plausible meanings of 'nit' still gives a decisive result.

operationalization: Compile host-parasite occurrence records for lice and ticks on birds, mammals and specifically Equus asinus. Any authenticated donkey louse or tick record refutes the exception; uninfested host species test the broader universal.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: open species-interaction records including host-parasite associations

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
candidate_datasets.role: parasite occurrence records with host information in some datasets

obstacles: Absence of a parasite record is not evidence of true absence.
Host-parasite records are geographically and taxonomically biased.
Domestic treatment suppresses modern infestations.
rationale: Positive infestation records are decisive counterexamples and are available in public interaction data. The universal infestation clause cannot be confirmed from presence-only, unevenly sampled records.

operationalization: Track Blastophaga psenes emergence from caprifigs, entry into receptive cultivated figs, pollination and subsequent fruit retention. Exclusion and introduction comparisons test whether wasp entry increases retention and explains caprification.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: open fig-fig-wasp interaction records

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
candidate_datasets.role: occurrence records for Ficus carica and Blastophaga psenes

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: DNA barcodes for fig-wasp identification

obstacles: Fruit retention can also depend on cultivar and parthenocarpy.
rationale: The life-cycle sequence and effect on fruit set are standard, measurable aspects of caprification with extensive existing agronomic and interaction data. Comparison across pollination-dependent and parthenocarpic cultivars can address the main confound.

operationalization: Compile reproductive anatomy and birth records for candidate vipers, scoring internal eggs, live birth, litter size and duration of parturition, and compare modes across other snakes. The internal-egg/live-birth sequence supports ovoviviparity; contradictory litter or timing records refute numerical details.

candidate_datasets.name: Reptile Database
candidate_datasets.role: public snake taxonomy and reproductive references

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open reproductive and life-history traits for animals

obstacles: The historical viper species is not uniquely identified.
Older 'ovoviviparity' terminology can obscure placental viviparity.
Birth timing is less widely recorded than reproductive mode.
rationale: Reproductive mode and litter size are standard snake traits with broad existing records. The one-day and approximately twenty offspring clauses have sparser data, but the central internal-egg/live-birth claim is directly resolvable.
